Accurate and honestly disclosed. Reviewer judgment on point (3): the carry-back is faithful to D-232 at GICS industry and sector level but not at sub-industry level. On 374 funded ICB-era rows (172 previously blank, 202 previously in another industry) gics_sub_industry is the single label the shared map gives the printed industry heading. The filer never printed that sub-industry. Examples: 'Hotels, Restaurants & Leisure' becomes Hotels, Resorts & Cruise Lines for Lakeland Tours and Azzurri; 'Financial Services' becomes Diversified Financial Services for Neon Maple, a payments business; 'Software' becomes Application Software. So the step does invent sub-industry specificity. Mitigating: (i) the build already publishes exactly this representative on the same companies' rows from 2025-12-31, since every later heading maps to one label, so the carried rows add no new kind of error; (ii) industry and sector are right where 202 rows were in the wrong industry before; (iii) more specific labels inside the heading are kept (339 rows), as the ruling asks. Risk: the public industry time series (pipeline/export/timeseries_exports.py) uses gics_sub_industry as its label, so the false precision reaches the site. The proposed industry-level marker or gics_industry column is the right fix, and the owner should be told the 374 rows are industry-level. Counts reproduced from carry_buckets_rfhcf.txt: 172 + 202 = 374, 46 + 46 = 92, 339 kept; 218 filled matches the reviewer's own count.
